name: lab_agent_burst_v1
description: Four small-lab users each run one closed-loop agent session. Starts are slightly staggered, while tool-result turns create repeatable prefill bursts during ongoing decode.
rationale: Four independent users are enough to create overlap without turning the workload into an open-loop saturation test.
The 0/50/100/150 ms starts model users entering the service close together rather than at an artificial barrier.
Each later request waits for that user's prior request to finish and then waits a fixed user-specific think time, preserving closed-loop agent behavior.
The main profile uses 512 decode tokens because a shorter decode would overstate how often prefill arrives relative to decode in the target AIME-like agent workload.
Fixed assistant transcripts and fixed tool results, rather than each policy's actual output, make every submitted prompt token-identical across policies even when generated outputs disagree.

content_materialization.tokenizer_requirement: Materialize and validate every segment with the same public tokenizer used by the served model.
content_materialization.representation: Text submitted to the public API, with verified token IDs used only for materialization validation.
content_materialization.method: Construct deterministic tokenizer-stable project-context, assistant-transcript, and tool-result text from this seed; tokenize without added special tokens; before submitting text, require every segment and nested prompt to encode to exactly the requested valid non-special token IDs and decode back to identical text.
content_materialization.session_isolation: Give each user's initial prompt a distinct first token so separate sessions cannot share a radix prefix.
content_materialization.fixed_input_rule: For turn t>0, submit the prior fixed prompt text followed by the prior turn's pre-generated fixed assistant transcript text and the new pre-generated fixed tool-result text. Never append the policy's actual generated output to a later prompt.
content_materialization.repetition_seed_rule: segment_materialization_seed = 20260825 + 10000 * repetition_index; request_seed remains fixed by user and turn so every policy receives identical seeds

closed_loop_submission.input_dependency: Later prompts use only pre-generated fixed transcript/tool text whose tokenization was verified; actual response completion controls timing but actual response text never controls later input.

stress_short_turn_192.label: stress_short_turn_192
stress_short_turn_192.purpose: Optional short-turn stress exploration only; it must not support the main performance conclusion because it raises prefill arrival frequency relative to decode.

request_contract.output_mismatch_behavior: Record exact output mismatch against the reference policy and continue all remaining requests.

metrics.timestamp_source: Client-side time.perf_counter relative to benchmark start; submitted_at is captured immediately before constructing and sending the HTTP request.
metrics.saved_stream_events: Save the timestamp and text of every non-empty SSE choice text event, plus the total count of SSE events containing a choice.
metrics.ttft_seconds: First non-empty SSE text-event timestamp minus the client-side request submission timestamp; this includes HTTP connection/setup time and service-side queueing before the first token.
metrics.tpot_seconds: Client-observed (last non-empty SSE text-event timestamp - first non-empty SSE text-event timestamp) / (usage.completion_tokens - 1); by the standard TPOT definition, pre-first-token queueing is represented in TTFT rather than TPOT.
metrics.sse_text_event_gap_seconds: Adjacent non-empty SSE text-event timestamp gaps, summarized per request at P50/P95/P99/max. These are not called token gaps unless the event count equals usage.completion_tokens.
metrics.stream_granularity_check: Cross-check non-empty SSE text-event count against usage.completion_tokens; retain TPOT based on completion_tokens even when the public stream coalesces tokens.
metrics.makespan_seconds: last response completion timestamp minus benchmark start for all 20 requests
metrics.prompt_throughput_tokens_per_second: sum of usage.prompt_tokens across all 20 requests divided by makespan_seconds
metrics.actual_new_prefill_throughput_tokens_per: sum of (usage.prompt_tokens - cached_tokens) across all 20 requests divided by makespan_seconds; unlike prompt throughput this excludes reused prefix tokens
metrics.decode_throughput_tokens_per_second: sum of usage.completion_tokens across all 20 requests divided by makespan_seconds
metrics.actual_new_prefill_tokens: usage.prompt_tokens - cached_tokens; compare to 640 on turn 0 and 832 on later main-profile turns
metrics.prefix_cache_validation: For each later turn, require cached_tokens to equal the complete prior fixed prompt length; require each turn's actual_new_prefill_tokens to equal the profile expectation.
metrics.output_consistency: Compare each actual output with the same user/turn reference output, record the first difference, and never terminate timing early solely for a mismatch.
